in_sanskrit.name: अनन्थ
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Anantha is derived from the Sanskrit word अनन्थ (anantha), which means 'endless, infinite, boundless'. This name is often used to refer to the infinite, endless, and boundless aspects of the divine. In Hindu mythology, Anantha is the name of the divine serpent, Vasuki, who is the king of all serpents and lies at the base of the cosmic mountain, Mount Meru. He is also the support of the universe, as the ocean of milk, Ksheerasagara, rests on his numerous hoods.

This name is a symbol of stability and protection, and Anantha is often invoked in our traditional prayers and mantras for the well-being and prosperity of one's life.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Anantha represents the limitless and infinite nature of the Divine. As a name that signifies boundlessness, it is believed to ward off obstacles and bestow blessings of direction, guidance, and growth. vedic_reference.note: The name Anantha is a significant name in Hindu mythology and is associated with the divine serpent, Vasuki, who is the king of all serpents and lies at the base of the cosmic mountain, Mount Meru. He is also the support of the universe, as the ocean of milk, Ksheerasagara, rests on his numerous hoods.

historical_references.reference: Anantha is a popular name for the Hindu deity Vishnu, who is often depicted reclining on the numerous coils of the serpent Anantashesha or Anantha Padmanabha. This symbolizes the infinite nature of Vishnu and his unending protection of the universe.

Anantha is also the name of a constellation in Indian astronomy, located in the northern celestial hemisphere. It is identified with the head of the serpent Ananta, who is said to hold the universe on his hoods.
